skill.name: deep-reading-analyst
skill.description: Analyze articles, papers, and long-form content with structured frameworks such as SCQA, 5W2H, critical thinking, inversion, mental models, and first principles.
skill.summary: Turn complex reading into structured analysis, practical insight, and clear next actions.

content.value_statement: Long articles and papers can hide weak arguments, missing context, and unclear next steps. This skill applies structured thinking frameworks to produce clear summaries, critiques, and actions.
actual_capabilities: Selects quick, standard, deep, or research analysis depth based on the user goal.
Applies SCQA and 5W2H to identify structure, core questions, and information gaps.
Evaluates arguments with critical thinking, inversion, evidence checks, and alternative perspectives.
Uses mental models, first principles, systems thinking, and Six Hats for deeper interpretation.
Produces study notes, decision frameworks, writing references, and actionable takeaways.
Compares multiple sources when research mode and search tools are available.
limitations: Requires source text, a readable document, or an accessible link from the user.
Does not verify factual claims unless search or external research tools are available.
May become too broad if the user requests many frameworks at once.
Does not replace expert review for medical, legal, financial, or scientific decisions.

use_cases.title: Study A Research Paper
use_cases.description: Break down a dense paper into thesis, evidence, assumptions, limits, and test questions.

use_cases.title: Evaluate A Strategy Article
use_cases.description: Assess business advice with SCQA, inversion, mental models, and practical risk checks.

use_cases.title: Prepare Writing Notes
use_cases.description: Extract key arguments, useful evidence, counterpoints, and gaps for an essay or report.

prompt_templates.title: Quick Article Summary
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner analysis for a single article.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this article at quick depth. Use SCQA and 5W2H. Give the thesis, main gaps, top insights, and one next action.

prompt_templates.title: Critical Reading Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this content with critical thinking and inversion. Identify strong claims, weak evidence, hidden assumptions, failure modes, and safer conclusions.

prompt_templates.title: Deep Framework Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this paper deeply. Use SCQA, 5W2H, mental models, first principles, systems thinking, and Six Hats. Keep the output concise.

prompt_templates.title: Cross-Source Synthesis
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these sources. Map their claims, evidence, assumptions, disagreements, and unique contributions. End with an integrated view and open questions.

output_examples.input: A user shares a long strategy article about remote work adoption.
output: SCQA summary that separates background, problem, question, and proposed answer.
5W2H gap list covering missing stakeholder, timing, location, method, and cost details.
Inversion review with likely failure points and mitigation steps.
Three practical takeaways for the user context.

output_examples.input: A student asks for help understanding a research paper.
output: Plain-language thesis and key concept explanations.
Evidence map that separates data, interpretation, and assumptions.
First-principles breakdown of what must be true for the paper to hold.

output_examples.input: A manager compares several articles before making a decision.
output: Cross-source matrix of claims, evidence strength, and disagreement areas.
Mental-model analysis from economic, systems, and risk perspectives.
Decision guidance with benefits, risks, missing information, and next steps.

best_practices: State your reading goal and desired depth before analysis starts.
Provide the full source text when links may be inaccessible or gated.
Ask for fewer frameworks when you need a concise answer.
anti_patterns: Using every framework for a short or simple article.
Treating the analysis as fact-checking without external verification.
Requesting conclusions without sharing enough source material.

faq.question: What content works best with this skill?
faq.answer: It works best with articles, papers, reports, essays, strategy memos, and long-form educational content.

faq.question: Can it analyze multiple sources?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare sources and synthesize agreement, disagreement, gaps, and unique contributions.

faq.question: Does it fact-check claims automatically?
faq.answer: No. It analyzes structure and reasoning. Fact-checking requires accessible sources and available search tools.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it use?
faq.answer: It uses SCQA, 5W2H, critical thinking, inversion, mental models, first principles, systems thinking, and Six Hats.

faq.question: Can I request one specific framework?
faq.answer: Yes. You can ask for one framework, a named combination, or a depth level.

faq.question: Is it suitable for expert decisions?
faq.answer: It supports understanding and reasoning. It should not replace qualified expert review for high-stakes decisions.
